text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1.0,"launches":0.5,"pipeline":3.0,"footprint":1.0},"rationale":"Four attempts observed; all numerically passed, compiled, and simulator-completed, with actual smem pinned at exactly 32768 in every case, confirming the 32768-byte portability cap is binding and the estimate cannot discriminate tuples once saturated. Best simulated latency remains attempt-01 (128,64,32,2) at 2544.21 us; attempt-00 (128,64,64,1) at 2558.09 us; attempt-03 (64,128,32,2) at 2575.61 us; attempt-02 (64,128,64,1) at 2592.58 us. The only factor correlated with improvement is block_M=128 with block_K=32 and num_stages=2, i.e., deeper staging with smaller K-tile; both block_M=64 variants and both stages=1 variants were slower. Revision rationale: raise pipeline weight to 3.0 to strongly favor num_stages>=2 with block_K=32 (the observed winning direction), drop traffic to 1.0 because block_M=128/block_N=64 already dominates reuse and traffic did not track observed ranking, drop footprint to 1.0 since it is saturated and a weak discriminator, and keep launches at 0.5 to mildly favor block_M=128. Domains unchanged and full: no exclusion caused infeasibility and all tiles divide 4096; shared_memory_limit remains the hard 32768-byte portability cap. Previously evaluated tuples are excluded via the solver history mechanism to force a new point, so the next hypothesis targets untested deeper-staging tuples such as block_M=128 with num_stages=3 and block_K=32, or block_M=128/block_N=128 with num_stages=2/3, to see whether further pipeline depth under the cap lowers GB10 simulated latency. Validation scope: Metal executes the exact source/config/TIR but the CUDA binary is not executed; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements, and the dimensionless proxy is a ranking aid only, not a claim of global optimality."}
